cover.alt: A batter waits at the wicket as a bowler runs in on a sunny cricket ground.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Cricket is a sport played by two teams of eleven players. One team bats, and the other team bowls and fields. The game uses a bat, ball, pitch, and wickets. Teams score runs and play in three main match formats. This explainer has at least five short parts with an immediate guided check after each part, so you can learn one idea at a time.

items.prompt: Do you know any sport where one team bats and the other team bowls or pitches?
items.answer: Baseball is one example. Cricket is another. In both sports, one team tries to score and the other team tries to stop them.
items.explanation: This gets you thinking about bat-and-ball sports before we start.

items.prompt: How many players do you think are on one cricket team?
items.answer: There are eleven players on one cricket team.
items.explanation: Knowing the team size helps you picture the game.

items.prompt: Look at the word wicket. What do you think a wicket might be in a sport?
items.answer: A wicket in cricket is a target made of three stumps with two bails on top. The bowler tries to hit it.
items.explanation: This word is very important in cricket. You will learn more about it soon.

blocks.title: Part 1: The Teams and the Aim
paragraphs: Cricket is played by two teams. Each team has eleven players. One team bats. The other team fields and bowls. The batting team tries to score as many runs as possible. The fielding team tries to get the batters out. An innings can end when ten batters are out or when the team finishes its overs. Then the other team bats. The team with more runs usually wins.

blocks.title: Check: The Teams and the Aim

items.prompt: What does the batting team try to do, and what does the fielding team try to do?
items.answer: The batting team tries to score runs. The fielding team tries to get the batting players out.
items.explanation:
These are the two opposite goals of the game.

If you played cricket, would you rather bat or field? Why?

blocks.title: Part 2: The Pitch and the Wickets
paragraphs: The pitch is a flat strip of ground in the middle of the field. It is 22 yards long. At each end of the pitch there is a wicket. A wicket is made of three wooden sticks called stumps. Two small pieces of wood called bails sit on top of the stumps. The bowler stands at one end and sends the ball toward the wicket at the other end. The batter stands in front of their wicket to protect it.

images.alt: A top-down view of a cricket pitch with wickets and crease lines at both ends.

blocks.title: Check: The Pitch and the Wickets

items.prompt: What is a wicket made of, and why does the batter stand in front of it?
items.answer: A wicket is made of three stumps with two bails on top. The batter stands in front of it to protect it from the bowler.
items.explanation:
The wicket is the target. Protecting it is the batter's main job.

Why do you think the bails are important? What might happen if they fall off?

blocks.title: Part 3: Batting and Scoring Runs
paragraphs: The batter uses a flat bat to hit the ball. When the ball is hit, the two batters at the wickets can run to each other’s end. Each completed run adds one run to the score. If the ball reaches the boundary rope around the field, the batting team gets four runs without running. If the ball flies over the boundary without bouncing, the team gets six runs.

images.alt: Two batters run between the wickets while the ball rolls toward the boundary rope.

items.prompt: How does a team score six runs from one hit?
items.answer: The batter hits the ball and it flies over the boundary rope without bouncing. That scores six runs.
items.explanation:
A six is the biggest single score from one ball in cricket.

Do you think it is harder to score a four or a six? Why?

blocks.title: Part 4: Bowling and Overs
paragraphs: The bowler runs up and bowls the ball toward the batter. The ball may bounce once on the pitch before it reaches the batter. Six valid balls from one bowler make one over. After each over, a different bowler takes the ball from the other end. One bowler cannot bowl two overs in a row.

items.prompt: How many balls are in one over, and can the same bowler bowl two overs in a row?
items.answer: One over has six balls. The same bowler cannot bowl two overs in a row. A different bowler must take over.
items.explanation:
This rule keeps the game fair and means teams need several good bowlers.

Why do you think cricket uses the word over for a set of six balls?

blocks.title: Part 5: Common Ways to Get Out
paragraphs: There are several ways a batter can be dismissed. Bowled means the ball hits the stumps and the bails fall off. Caught means a fielder catches a ball hit by the bat before it touches the ground. Run out means the batter is outside the crease line when a fielder breaks the wicket with the ball during a run. Ten dismissals can end an innings.

blocks.title: Check: Common Ways to Get Out

items.prompt: What is the difference between being bowled and being caught?
items.answer: Bowled means the ball hits the stumps and the bails fall. Caught means a fielder catches the ball in the air before it touches the ground.
items.explanation:
Both end the batter's turn, but they happen in different ways.

Which dismissal do you think is the most exciting to watch? Why?

blocks.title: Part 6: The Three Formats
paragraphs: Cricket has three main formats. A Test match is the longest. Each team can bat in two innings, and the match can last up to five days. A One Day International, called an ODI, gives each team 50 overs to bat. An ODI usually finishes in one day. A Twenty20, called a T20, gives each team only 20 overs. A T20 match takes about three hours. The ICC Cricket World Cup uses ODI matches. The ICC Men’s T20 World Cup uses T20 matches.

images.alt: A visual comparison of Test, ODI, and T20 cricket by days, innings, overs, and hours.

items.prompt: How is a T20 match different from a Test match?
items.answer: A T20 match gives each team only 20 overs and finishes in about three hours. A Test match can last up to five days and each team bats twice.
items.explanation:
The number of overs decides how long the match takes.

Which format sounds most interesting to you, and why?

items.prompt: Imagine a friend asks you to explain cricket in three sentences. What would you say?
items.answer: Cricket is a sport with two teams of eleven players. One team bats to score runs while the other team bowls and fields to get batters out. Teams take turns to bat, and the team with the higher match score usually wins. A match can use the Test, ODI, or T20 format.
items.explanation: A good answer connects the aim, the players, and the formats in your own words.

rows.meaning: three wooden stumps with two bails on top; the target the bowler aims at
rows.example: The ball hit the wicket and the bails fell off.

rows.meaning: a set of six balls bowled by one bowler
rows.example: The bowler took two wickets in one over.

rows.meaning: points scored by the batting team
rows.example: The team scored 250 runs in their innings.

rows.meaning: the period when one team bats until ten players are out
rows.example: England scored 300 runs in their first innings.

rows.meaning: the rope around the edge of the field; hitting it scores four or six runs
rows.example: The ball rolled to the boundary for four runs.

rows.meaning: a way a batter gets out and their innings ends
rows.example: Being caught is one of the most common dismissals.

rows.meaning: the longest format of cricket, lasting up to five days
rows.example: The Test match between Australia and England lasted four days.

rows.meaning: the shortest main format, with twenty overs per team
rows.example: The T20 match finished in less than three hours.
